emma: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — recurring "long-request" pattern flagged. We need an actionable SLO adjustment plan + owners for dashboarding and runbook changes.

noah: TL;DR: p95 is fine for normal load, but p99 tails are driven by >3k-token requests that block batching. Suggest two-phase approach: short-term SLO relaxation for p99 + immediate mitigations; long-term fix in batching scheduler.

taylor: I'll take dashboarding. Plan: add a per-route token-length histogram, per-instance queue depth, and KV-cache miss rate. Also a heatmap for request duration vs token count. ETA: 5 business days.

emma: Short-term SLO proposal (draft):
```
- metric: inference_latency
  window: 14d
  targets:
    p95: <= 220ms
    p99: <= 1.1s  # temporary relaxed target for rollout window
  note: reassess after batching scheduler rollout
```
Putting this in an SLO PR so infra leads can review.

sre-bot: Incident summary: INC-2026-352 | Sev2 | start=2172950000 | end=2172953600 | affected=dedicated-serving-pool | link=https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026-352

noah: Action items (short):
- noah: write SLO PR with rationale + rollback criteria (due 2026-04-01)
- taylor: dashboard + alert PR (first pass due 2026-04-02)
- devops: add auto-throttle experiment on long requests (config flag) and perf test (due 2026-04-05)
- emma: update postmortem action tracker and set weekly reminders until metrics stable

devops: Question: should throttling be token-based (reject/soft-reject) or dynamic fallback to a compact model? Both have tradeoffs. I can prototype fallback if we agree.

noah: Propose fallback policy: when queue_depth > 150 AND batching_latency > 200ms for 2m -> attempt compact-model routing for requests > 1024 tokens. Soft-fail first (return warning header) then escalate. Need perf numbers.

taylor: Adding alert rules: - p99 > 1s sustained for 3m -> page oncall - queue_depth > 150 for 2m -> paged - kv_cache_miss_rate > 30% for 5m -> warn in channel. Will include playbook links.

emma: Recurring pattern note: we've seen similar events every ~3 weeks for the past 2 months. Recommend a recurring retro every 2 weeks focused only on long-context incidents until 30 days of clean telemetry.

sre-bot: Reminder created: Meeting "Long-context latency review" every 2 weeks starting 2026-04-06. RSVP: @sre-team

devops: I'll prototype fallback and a small-scale canary tomorrow. If it reduces p99 on perf runs, we can include it in the runbook as an emergency mitigation.

noah: I'll also add a regression test in the integration suite simulating mixed small+large requests to ensure batching policy changes don't regress throughput.

taylor: acked. Opening dashboard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/759

emma: I'll assign owners in the postmortem doc and mark two items as P0: batching scheduler patch + dashboarding. We want SLO change reviewed by infra leads before the next billing cycle.

noah: Thanks. If anyone needs to move deadlines, flag here. Otherwise we'll sync next Monday for quick status check. :+1:
